subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only per-agent tool policy, and which public config shape should own the split between requester-visible tools and child-inheritable tools?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change defines a new security boundary and public config contract that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that removes listed tools from the requester model surface while preserving explicit deny as an everywhere-deny and allowing controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Use the existing per-spawn `toolsAllow` direction for child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate agents or prompt guidance until a later design.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject delegate-only inheritance for now and document the security rationale plus the separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that removes listed tools from the requester model surface while preserving explicit deny as an everywhere-deny and allowing controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses subagent runtime, tool-policy, config, and security-boundary semantics where his history is the strongest available routing signal.
